summary_html: Agency places a child with **relatives or kin caregivers** instead of non-relative foster care. Federal law favors kinship care as least-restrictive, family-preserving placement.
authority_html:

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Vacating and remanding, the Court held that a circuit court denying placement with a grandparent must enter detailed findings showing it considered the statutory grandparent preference and determined, on the whole record, that the preference was overcome by the child's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: It is the current WV rule enforcing the grandparent placement preference in W. Va. Code § 49-4-114(a)(3).
key_cases.quote: in denying grandparent placement the circuit court must make detailed findings of fact and conclusions of law demonstrating that it considered the grandparent preference

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: The Court held that a minor over fourteen who nominates a relative as guardian does not thereby permit a court to divest his fit, non-offending biological mother of custody, although the child may be entitled to visitation with the grandmother.
key_cases.relevance: Kinship caregivers, even ones the child chooses, do not outrank a non-offending parent.
key_cases.quote: A court may not divest Gina H., Antonio's biological mother, of her custodial rights simply because Carol G. would be a "fit" guardian

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Affirming denial of a non-parent guardianship petition, the Court held that a court appointing a guardian under W. Va. Code § 44-10-3 must give priority to the child's mother or father, and that a family court presented with abuse and neglect allegations in a guardianship petition must refer the matter under Rule 48a(a).
key_cases.relevance: Kinship guardianship cannot displace a fit parent's statutory priority.
key_cases.quote: In appointing a guardian, the court shall give priority to the minor's mother or father

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Delaware Tribe of Indians v. Nowicki-Eldridge
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Granting a writ of prohibition, the Court rejected the 'existing Indian family' exception, held ICWA governed the proceeding, found no good cause to deny transfer, and directed the circuit court to transfer jurisdiction to the Delaware Tribe's district court.
key_cases.relevance: Prospective kinship placements are subordinate to a properly invoked tribal transfer under ICWA.
key_cases.quote: we find that the circuit court erred in denying the motion to transfer this action to the tribal court

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Holding that the lower tribunals abused their discretion by failing to apply the statutory grandparent preference, the Court remanded with directions that the child be placed with his paternal grandparents for adoption following a gradual transition of custody.
key_cases.relevance: It is the rule In re A.F. applies: the statutory grandparent preference is presumptively in the child's best interests and can be defeated only on the record as a whole, not on an adoption committee's unexplored misgivings.
key_cases.quote: the preference for grandparent placement may be overcome only where the record reviewed in its entirety establishes that such placement is not in the best interests of the child

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Denying the requested writ with directions, the Court held that custody was properly restored to the fit natural father over the stepfather who had been caring for the child, and directed the circuit court to confer visitation on the stepfather and half-brother with whom the child had formed close bonds.
key_cases.relevance: It is the rule underlying both In re Jonathan G. and In re Antonio R.A.: a kin or de facto caregiver's attachment to the child cannot displace a parent who has not been shown unfit, abandoning, immoral or otherwise derelict.
key_cases.quote: There being no showing of unfitness or abandonment before us, we find that the circuit court did not err in restoring the custody of Elizabeth to her natural father
